decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up left approach to the rear-left tube, lifting and orienting gradually; right arm stays home.
Move left wrist above the rear-left tube, aligning gripper long axis with its observed tilt. Maintain elbow-up continuity.
Complete overhead alignment and descend toward the tube body with open fingers; inspect centering before grasp.
Shift grasp toward the cap-side body using wrist view, then close left fingers fully around the first tube.
Lift the first tube clear with the gripper held closed; check visual retention before rotating upright.
Transport the retained first tube toward the rack while rotating upright in small continuous increments.
Continue rotating the tube toward vertical above the left-side rack slots, keeping it well clear of the rack.
Finish upright orientation and align over a left rack opening, accounting for the wrist-to-finger offset.
Lower the upright first tube toward the left rack opening, retaining the grasp and checking alignment before final insertion.
Insert the first tube further vertically at low speed, keeping the same lateral alignment and closed grasp.
Tube appears to contact the near rack edge rather than enter. Lift slightly and shift forward toward the visible left large opening before retrying.
Retry slow vertical insertion after forward alignment; monitor the tube base against the opening.
Release the first tube over the aligned opening to let it seat, then withdraw slightly for an unobstructed visual check.
Withdraw the open fingers and allow the released tube to settle; it currently appears tilted and needs verification.
The first tube remained tilted. Approach its upper body with fingers open and a matching tilt to regrasp and reseat it.
Lower open fingers toward the tilted tube's cap-side body for a corrective grasp.
Center around the tilted tube's upper body and close for a corrective lift; alignment remains uncertain.
Lift the regrasped tube above the rack before correcting its observed lean; retain closed fingers.
Straighten the retained tube above the rack, adding clearance while removing the wrist tilt.
Correct the remaining tube lean visible relative to the fingers and lower toward the left large opening.
Lift clear and choose the more visible central large opening rather than continue pressing at the uncertain left opening.
Fine-align the tube with the central large slot and lower slowly, using the cap and hole projection.
The wrist view shows the large opening just in front of the tube base. Lift slightly, shift toward that opening, and retry without forcing contact.
Lower into the now-centered large opening in small vertical increments, retaining the tube until seating is checked.
The cone is visibly on the rack web, not seated. Lift and move forward toward the large central opening, then approach gently.
The large opening is now visible around the cone. Lower vertically in small increments to seat the first tube.
Stop pressing against the rim. Lift, shift the cone slightly farther into the visible opening, and reapproach.
Lower toward the clearly visible large hole beneath the cone, adding only a small rightward centering correction.
Fingers appear to limit descent against the rack. Open over the large opening and retreat to let the tube seat under gravity.
Clear the rack with open fingers and let the released tube settle before reassessing its depth and uprightness.
The released tube is perched between large slots. Approach higher on its body to regrasp without the fingers striking the rack.
Close around the standing tube and make a small test lift to verify the corrective grasp before translating to a large slot.
The test lift missed the tube. Reopen and lower the fingers around its body for a visually confirmed grasp.
Advance the open fingers toward the standing tube's upper body; the wrist view indicates it is still beyond the grasp.
Finish advancing around the upper tube body and close gently for a higher grasp, keeping clearance from the rack.
Test-lift the new high grasp so the tube can be repositioned with its bottom clear and fingers above the rack.
Move the retained high grasp from the small/web location toward the adjacent large opening on its left and begin lowering.
Continue a slow vertical seating motion with the cap grasp, stopping to inspect for contact or sliding.
Release at the new large-slot position and clear the view to determine whether the tube is seated or still resting on the rim.
Withdraw fully to inspect the first tube's slot and make clearance for the next approach; its seating remains uncertain.
Begin an overhead approach to the remaining left tube, rotating gradually above the table while leaving the rack untouched.
Rotate farther overhead and descend toward the second tube, aligning with its diagonal axis.
Fine-align the overhead fingers with the second tube and lower to body-grasp height.
Align the fingers with the tube's visible axis and close around its cap-side body.
Lift the second tube clear of the table with the left gripper closed before transporting it upright.
Rotate the retained second tube toward upright above the table, maintaining clearance from the first tube and rack.
Finish bringing the second tube upright above the left-front rack area, retaining clearance for alignment.
Bring the upright second tube down over the left-front large slot with a small forward alignment adjustment.
Lower the second tube carefully toward seating depth, with a small forward centering adjustment.
The second tube has slid against the near rim. Lift briefly and shift forward into the left-front large slot rather than press down.
